_about.artifact: contracts/rules.json — the governance rules, one file for the whole system
_about.authoredOrGenerated: AUTHORED — and it is THE ONLY PLACE A RULE IS EDITED. Rules carrying publishTo are emitted verbatim into the consumer-facing views by scripts/build-dc-rules.mjs (between generated-block markers in claude-design/readme.md and Design System Guide.md); --check is in yarn check:drift. This single-source design exists because the rules were previously hand-maintained in three places and drifted into two live contradictions that both shipped.
_about.purpose: The rules consumer agents must follow when generating pages/designs with UIDS — the 'constitution' the judge scores against.

audiences.consumer agent: primary — these rules ARE its governance. Claude Design sessions receive the publishTo rules via the injected readme.md; in-repo agents read this file first per catalog.json's readingOrder.
audiences.builder agent: edits rules here (never in a generated view) and keeps judge.mjs's check-to-rule-id mapping in step when a rule id changes — check-judge-rules.mjs will not let it forget.
audiences.checkers: scripts/build-dc-rules.mjs publishes the publishTo rules; scripts/build-catalog.mjs links to this file and counts rules.rules.length; scripts/check-judge-rules.mjs binds judge.mjs's rule-id vocabulary to this file's ids. CORRECTED 2026-08-22: an earlier draft said judge.mjs 'names a rule id from this file in every violation it reports'. The 'names a rule id' half was right; the implied enforcement was not. judge.mjs did build `const ruleById = new Map(...)` and never reference it — dead code — so renaming an id here broke every judge report silently. FIXED the same day: the dead Map is gone (judge.mjs never needed the rule DATA, only the ids) and check-judge-rules.mjs, in yarn check:drift, now derives the ids out of judge.mjs's source and fails unless each is either in this file or a declared view-local rule. judge.mjs's `no-bare-element-styles` is the one such exemption — a view-local claude-design rule, correctly scoped per scopeRule below, documented in eval/README.md and enforced by check-claude-design.mjs — and the exemption is itself checked (it must still be emitted, must NOT appear in this file, and must name a view and a checker that exist). So renaming a rule here NOW fails check:drift, which is the signal to update judge.mjs and re-score the eval fixtures.

_about.scopeRule: A rule that describes a single VIEW's own mechanics does NOT belong here — it belongs in that view. (Example: 'no bare element selectors' is about dc-import's shared cascade; it lives in claude-design/readme.md and check-claude-design.mjs enforces it there.) A view-local rule is also the only legitimate reason judge.mjs may emit an id absent from this file, so each one is declared in check-judge-rules.mjs's VIEW_LOCAL with the view that owns it — an undeclared id is an error, not an exception.
moreInfo: contracts/README.md — 'The agent catalog' section documents the rules pipeline and the drift incident that motivated it
eval/README.md — how judge.mjs maps its checks to these rule ids, and the note on how that mapping is enforced
scripts/build-dc-rules.mjs — the publisher; scripts/judge.mjs — the enforcer; scripts/check-judge-rules.mjs — what keeps the two vocabularies in step

id.purpose: Stable kebab-case rule id. judge.mjs reports violations by this id — renaming or removing one requires a matching judge.mjs update AND a matching row in eval/README.md's check-to-rule table. check-judge-rules.mjs fails until both are done, so the update is a to-do list rather than something to remember; then re-score the eval fixtures.
consumedBy: check-judge-rules.mjs (as the authority judge.mjs's emitted ids are checked against)
judge.mjs (emits these ids as string literals; it does NOT read this file — the coupling is static, checked, and deliberately one-way)
id.notConsumedBy: build-catalog.mjs reads rules.rules.length and a hardcoded path (lines 138, 186, 193) — it never reads an individual rule id.

enforcement.purpose: 'judge' = mechanically checkable (a script or the Figma readback can verify it) | 'agent' = guidance an agent must follow but only human review fully verifies.
consumedBy: build-dc-rules.mjs (published verbatim into the views as '**id** (enforcement) — ')
enforcement.notConsumedBy: judge.mjs. An earlier draft claimed 'only judge-tier rules produce scored violations' — it reads as a mechanism and is not one, because judge.mjs does not read this file at all. The tiers also do not line up with what the judge emits: 'judge' means mechanically checkable BY SOMETHING, and respect-breakpoint-modes is judge-tier but enforced by check-figma, while three 'agent' rules are partly checkable and scored advisory. That is why check-judge-rules.mjs asserts emitted ⊆ ids and NOT enforcement-tier ⊆ emitted.

rule.purpose: The rule text, written TO the consuming agent. May carry its own correction history inline when the previous wording actively caused harm (see page-heading-structure — the corrected rule records what the wrong version broke, so it cannot be innocently restored).
consumedBy: build-dc-rules.mjs (published verbatim — no paraphrasing in views)

publishTo.purpose: Which generated views must carry the rule verbatim ('claude-design' = readme.md + Design System Guide.md). Rules WITHOUT publishTo are repo-facing only — e.g. respect-breakpoint-modes, which is about authoring Figma variants and means nothing to a page-building agent.

rules.rule: Every color, font family, font weight, and font size must come from a token in catalog/tokens.json. No raw hex values or ad-hoc type sizes where a token exists.

In Figma, component breakpoint variants must pin the Components collection mode (mobile / md (980) / page (1350)) and the Semantic collection mode (small (600) for Mobile/MD, large (1310) for Page). Dimension tokens with value 0 mean auto/content-driven — do not bind them.
